title: ज्यानको बाजी लगाएर साउदीमा रोजगारी गर्न बाध्य नेपाली, नेपालबाट कामदार जान रोकिन्छन् ?
content:
No ads found for this position काठमाडौं । मध्यपूर्व क्षेत्रमा सुरक्षाको संवेदनशीलता दिनप्रतिदिन बढ्दै गइरहेको छ । साउदी अरबमा पनि पछिल्लो समय आक्रमणका घटनाहरू भइरहेका छन् । नेपालबाट करिब ४ लाख श्रमिकले मध्यपूर्वको प्रमुख गन्तव्य साउदी अरबमा काम गरिरहेका छन् । वार्षिक रूपमा करिब ९० हजारको हाराहारीमा नेपालीहरू साउदीमा काम गर्न जाने गरेका छन् । साउदी अरबको पूर्वी प्रान्तस्थित सैबाह तेल क्षेत्रमा काम गर्ने क्रममा ड्रोन आक्रमणमा परि एक नेपालीको मृत्यु भइसकेको छ । साउदीमा शृङ्खलाबद्ध आक्रमणहरू बढ्दै गएका कारण त्यहाँ हाल कार्यरत नेपाली कामदारहरू पनि ठूलो जोखिममा रहेका छन् । नेपालबाट साउदी गएर काम गरिरहेका श्रमिकहरूको सुरक्षाका लागि सरकारले विभिन्न तहमा पहल गरिरहेको छ । युद्ध चर्किँदै जाँदा नेपाली कामदार पठाउने वा रोक्ने विषयमा हालसम्म कुनै पनि औपचारिक निर्णय भइसकेको छैन । परराष्ट्र मन्त्रालय र श्रम मन्त्रालयले यस विषयमा आन्तरिक रूपमा छलफल तथा अध्ययन गरिरहेका छन् । चाडपर्वको बिदाका कारण सरकार र म्यानपावर व्यवसायीहरू बीच कामदार पठाउने वा रोक्ने सन्दर्भमा औपचारिक छलफल हुन पाएको छैन । दशैँ अगाडिसम्म पनि नेपाली कामदारहरू साउदी अरब जाने क्रम जारी नै थियो । वैदेशिक रोजगार व्यवसायी संघका अध्यक्ष डिकबहादुर खत्रीका अनुसार अहिलेसम्म सरकारले साउदीमा कामदार पठाउने कार्य रोक्ने वा के गर्ने लगायतको विषयमा विषयमा कुनै ठोस छलफल गरेको छैन । उनले भने, ‘चाडपर्वको कारणले पनि हाल छलफल नभएको र अब सरकारसँग यस विषयमा छलफल हुने छ । साउदी अरब नेपालका लागि अत्यन्तै ठूलो श्रम बजार हो । जहाँ वार्षिक रूपमा करिब ९० हजारसम्म नेपालीहरू रोजगारीका लागि जाने र करिब ४ लाख श्रमिकले प्रत्यक्ष रूपमा काम गरिरहेका छन् ।’ संयुक्त राष्ट्रसंघ वा अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय सुरक्षा संयन्त्रले साउदी अरबलाई पूर्ण रूपमा रेड जोन (अति जोखिमयुक्त क्षेत्र) घोषणा नगरेसम्म यसलाई आधिकारिक रूपमा पूर्ण खतरायुक्त क्षेत्र भन्न नमिल्ने व्यवसायीहरूको तर्क रहेको छ । वैदेशिक रोजगार विभागका महानिर्देशक नवराज ढकालले साउदीमा नेपाली कामदार पठाउने कार्य रोक्ने वा अन्य कदम चाल्ने विषयमा हालसम्म ठोस निर्णय नभएको बताए । तर, परराष्ट्र र श्रम मन्त्रालयले यस विषयमा गम्भीरताका साथ अध्ययन गरिरहेको जानकारी दिए । महानिर्देशक ढकालका अनुसार साउदी अरेबियामा भइरहेको आक्रमण र युद्धका विषयमा मन्त्रालयले त्यहाँ नेपालीहरुको उपस्थिति र प्रवाह कस्तो छ भन्ने बारेमा लगातार अध्ययन गरिरहेको छ । पछिल्लो समय यस विषयमा थप नयाँ किसिमको कुनै पनि निर्णय नभएको र घटना कुन तहसम्म पुग्छ, त्यसको गम्भीरता र अवस्था हेरेर मात्र सरकारले आगामी कदम चाल्ने उहाँको भनाइ छ । साउदीमा भइरहेको यो युद्ध र द्वन्द्व कुनै नयाँ विषय नभई विगत दुई वर्षदेखि नै निरन्तर रूपमा चलिरहेको छ । युद्ध तथा आक्रमणको उच्च जोखिम हुँदाहुँदै पनि मुलुक भित्रको गरिबी र जीवनयापनको गम्भीर आर्थिक बाध्यताका कारण नेपालीहरू आफ्नो ज्यानको समेत परवाह नगरी वैदेशिक रोजगारीमा जान बाध्य भइरहेका छन् । सरकारले सुरक्षा अवस्थालाई मध्यनजर गर्दै आगामी दिनमा कस्तो रणनीति अपनाउँछ र अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय परिस्थिति कसरी अगाडि बढ्छ, त्यसले साउदी जाने लाखौँ नेपालीहरुको भविष्य निर्धारण गर्नेछ । Kathmandu. The security sensitivity in the Middle East region is increasing day by day. There have been recent incidents of attacks in Saudi Arabia as well. About 400,000 Nepali workers are working in Saudi Arabia, a major destination in the Middle East. About 90,000 Nepalis go to work in Saudi Arabia annually. A Nepali worker has been killed in a drone attack while working in the Saibah oil field in the Eastern Province of Saudi Arabia. Nepali workers currently working in Saudi Arabia are also at great risk due to the increasing number of attacks. The government is taking initiatives at various levels to ensure the safety of Nepali workers working in Saudi Arabia. As the war intensifies, no formal decision has been made yet on whether to send or stop Nepali workers. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Ministry of Labor are discussing and studying this issue internally. Due to the festive holidays, there has been no formal discussion between the government and manpower professionals regarding sending or stopping workers. Even before Dashain, the number of Nepali workers going to Saudi Arabia continued. According to Dik Bahadur Khatri, president of the Foreign Employment Entrepreneurs Association, the government has not yet held any concrete discussions on whether to stop sending workers to Saudi Arabia or what to do. He said, "Due to the festive season, there has been no discussion at present and now there will be discussions with the government on this issue. Saudi Arabia is a very large labor market for Nepal. Where about 90,000 Nepalis go for employment annually and about 400,000 workers are working directly." Businessmen argue that Saudi Arabia cannot be officially called a full-threat zone until the United Nations or international security mechanisms declare it a full-threat zone. Director General of the Department of Foreign Employment, Nawaraj Dhakal, said that no concrete decision has been made yet on stopping the sending of Nepali workers to Saudi Arabia or taking any other steps. However, he informed that the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Labor is seriously studying the issue. According to Director General Dhakal, the ministry is continuously studying the presence and flow of Nepalis there regarding the ongoing attacks and war in Saudi Arabia. He said that there has been no new decision on this issue recently and the government will take further steps only after considering the seriousness and situation of the incident. This war and conflict in Saudi Arabia is not a new issue, but has been ongoing for the past two years. Despite the high risk of war and attack, Nepalis are being forced to go abroad for employment without even caring for their lives due to poverty and severe economic constraints within the country. The future of millions of Nepalis traveling to Saudi Arabia will be determined by the strategy the government adopts in the coming days, keeping in mind the security situation, and how the international situation progresses.

पाएको छैन । दशैँ अगाडिसम्म पनि नेपाली कामदारहरू साउदी अरब जाने क्रम जारी नै थियो । वैदेशिक रोजगार व्यवसायी संघका अध्यक्ष डिकबहादुर खत्रीका अनुसार अहिलेसम्म सरकारले साउदीमा कामदार पठाउने कार्य रोक्ने वा के गर्ने लगायतको विषयमा विषयमा कुनै ठोस छलफल गरेको छैन । उनले भने, ‘चाडपर्वको कारणले पनि हाल छलफल नभएको र अब सरकारसँग यस विषयमा छलफल हुने छ । साउदी अरब नेपालका लागि अत्यन्तै ठूलो श्रम बजार हो । जहाँ वार्षिक रूपमा करिब ९० हजारसम्म नेपालीहरू रोजगारीका लागि जाने र करिब ४ लाख श्रमिकले प्रत्यक्ष रूपमा काम गरिरहेका छन् ।’ संयुक्त राष्ट्रसंघ वा अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय सुरक्षा संयन्त्रले साउदी अरबलाई पूर्ण रूपमा रेड जोन (अति जोखिमयुक्त क्षेत्र) घोषणा नगरेसम्म यसलाई आधिकारिक रूपमा पूर्ण खतरायुक्त क्षेत्र भन्न नमिल्ने व्यवसायीहरूको तर्क रहेको छ । वैदेशिक रोजगार विभागका महानिर्देशक नवराज ढकालले साउदीमा नेपाली कामदार पठाउने कार्य रोक्ने वा अन्य कदम चाल्ने विषयमा हालसम्म ठोस निर्णय नभएको बताए । तर, परराष्ट्र र श्रम मन्त्रालयले यस विषयमा गम्भीरताका साथ अध्ययन गरिरहेको जानकारी दिए । महानिर्देशक ढकालका अनुसार साउदी अरेबियामा भइरहेको आक्रमण र युद्धका विषयमा मन्त्रालयले त्यहाँ नेपालीहरुको उपस्थिति र प्रवाह कस्तो छ भन्ने बारेमा लगातार अध्ययन गरिरहेको छ । पछिल्लो समय यस विषयमा थप नयाँ किसिमको कुनै पनि निर्णय नभएको र घटना कुन तहसम्म पुग्छ, त्यसको गम्भीरता र अवस्था हेरेर मात्र सरकारले आगामी कदम चाल्ने उहाँको भनाइ छ । साउदीमा भइरहेको यो युद्ध र द्वन्द्व कुनै नयाँ विषय नभई विगत दुई वर्षदेखि नै निरन्तर रूपमा चलिरहेको छ । युद्ध तथा आक्रमणको उच्च जोखिम हुँदाहुँदै पनि मुलुक भित्रको गरिबी र जीवनयापनको गम्भीर आर्थिक बाध्यताका कारण नेपालीहरू आफ्नो ज्यानको समेत परवाह नगरी वैदेशिक रोजगारीमा जान बाध्य भइरहेका छन् । सरकारले सुरक्षा अवस्थालाई मध्यनजर गर्दै आगामी दिनमा कस्तो रणनीति अपनाउँछ र अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय परिस्थिति कसरी अगाडि बढ्छ, त्यसले साउदी जाने लाखौँ नेपालीहरुको भविष्य निर्धारण गर्नेछ । Kathmandu. The security sensitivity in the Middle East region is increasing day by day. There have been recent incidents of attacks in Saudi Arabia as well. About 400,000 Nepali workers are working in Saudi Arabia, a major destination in the Middle East. About 90,000 Nepalis go to work in Saudi Arabia annually. A Nepali worker has been killed in a drone attack while working in the Saibah oil field in the Eastern Province of Saudi Arabia. Nepali workers currently working in Saudi Arabia are also at great risk due to the increasing number of attacks. The government is taking initiatives at various levels to ensure the safety of Nepali workers working in Saudi Arabia. As the war intensifies, no formal decision has been made yet on whether to send or stop Nepali workers. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Ministry of Labor are discussing and studying this issue internally. Due to the festive holidays, there has been no formal discussion between the government and manpower professionals regarding sending or stopping workers. Even before Dashain, the number of Nepali workers going to Saudi Arabia continued. According to Dik Bahadur Khatri, president of the Foreign Employment Entrepreneurs Association, the government has not yet held any concrete discussions on whether to stop sending workers to Saudi Arabia or what to do. He said, "Due to the festive season, there has been no discussion at present and now there will be discussions with the government on this issue. Saudi Arabia is a very large labor market for Nepal. Where about 90,000 Nepalis go for employment annually and about 400,000 workers are working directly." Businessmen argue that Saudi Arabia cannot be officially called a full-threat zone until the United Nations or international security mechanisms declare it a full-threat zone. Director General of the Department of Foreign Employment, Nawaraj Dhakal, said that no concrete decision has been made yet on stopping the sending of Nepali workers to Saudi Arabia or taking any other steps. However, he informed that the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Labor is seriously studying the issue. According to Director General Dhakal, the ministry is continuously studying the presence and flow of Nepalis there regarding the ongoing attacks and war in Saudi Arabia. He said that there has been no new decision on this issue recently and the government will take further steps only after considering the seriousness and situation of the incident. This war and conflict in Saudi Arabia is not a new issue, but has been ongoing for the past two years. Despite the high risk of war and attack, Nepalis are being forced to go abroad for employment without even caring for their lives due to poverty and severe economic constraints within the country. The future of millions of Nepalis traveling to Saudi Arabia will be determined by the strategy the government adopts in the coming days, keeping in mind the security situation, and how the international situation progresses.

रूपमा रेड जोन (अति जोखिमयुक्त क्षेत्र) घोषणा नगरेसम्म यसलाई आधिकारिक रूपमा पूर्ण खतरायुक्त क्षेत्र भन्न नमिल्ने व्यवसायीहरूको तर्क रहेको छ । वैदेशिक रोजगार विभागका महानिर्देशक नवराज ढकालले साउदीमा नेपाली कामदार पठाउने कार्य रोक्ने वा अन्य कदम चाल्ने विषयमा हालसम्म ठोस निर्णय नभएको बताए । तर, परराष्ट्र र श्रम मन्त्रालयले यस विषयमा गम्भीरताका साथ अध्ययन गरिरहेको जानकारी दिए । महानिर्देशक ढकालका अनुसार साउदी अरेबियामा भइरहेको आक्रमण र युद्धका विषयमा मन्त्रालयले त्यहाँ नेपालीहरुको उपस्थिति र प्रवाह कस्तो छ भन्ने बारेमा लगातार अध्ययन गरिरहेको छ । पछिल्लो समय यस विषयमा थप नयाँ किसिमको कुनै पनि निर्णय नभएको र घटना कुन तहसम्म पुग्छ, त्यसको गम्भीरता र अवस्था हेरेर मात्र सरकारले आगामी कदम चाल्ने उहाँको भनाइ छ । साउदीमा भइरहेको यो युद्ध र द्वन्द्व कुनै नयाँ विषय नभई विगत दुई वर्षदेखि नै निरन्तर रूपमा चलिरहेको छ । युद्ध तथा आक्रमणको उच्च जोखिम हुँदाहुँदै पनि मुलुक भित्रको गरिबी र जीवनयापनको गम्भीर आर्थिक बाध्यताका कारण नेपालीहरू आफ्नो ज्यानको समेत परवाह नगरी वैदेशिक रोजगारीमा जान बाध्य Kathmandu. The security sensitivity in the Middle East region is increasing day by day. There have been recent incidents of attacks in Saudi Arabia as well. About 400,000 Nepali workers are working in Saudi Arabia, a major destination in the Middle East. About 90,000 Nepalis go to work in Saudi Arabia annually. A Nepali worker has been killed in a drone attack while working in the Saibah oil field in the Eastern Province of Saudi Arabia. Nepali workers currently working in Saudi Arabia are also at great risk due to the increasing number of attacks. The government is taking initiatives at various levels to ensure the safety of Nepali workers working in Saudi Arabia. As the war intensifies, no formal decision has been made yet on whether to send or stop Nepali workers. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Ministry of Labor are discussing and studying this issue internally. Due to the festive holidays, there has been no formal discussion between the government and manpower professionals regarding sending or stopping workers. Even before Dashain, the number of Nepali workers going to Saudi Arabia continued. According to Dik Bahadur Khatri, president of the Foreign Employment Entrepreneurs Association, the government has not yet held any concrete discussions on whether to stop sending workers to Saudi Arabia or what to do. He said, "Due to the festive season, there has been no discussion at present and now there will be discussions with the government on this issue. Saudi Arabia is a very large labor market for Nepal. Where about 90,000 Nepalis go for employment annually and about 400,000 workers are working directly." Businessmen argue that Saudi Arabia cannot be officially called a full-threat zone until the United Nations or international security mechanisms declare it a full-threat zone. Director General of the Department of Foreign Employment, Nawaraj Dhakal, said that no concrete decision has been made yet on stopping the sending of Nepali workers to Saudi Arabia or taking any other steps. However, he informed that the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Labor is seriously studying the issue. According to Director General Dhakal, the ministry is continuously studying the presence and flow of Nepalis there regarding the ongoing attacks and war in Saudi Arabia. He said that there has been no new decision on this issue recently and the government will take further steps only after considering the seriousness and situation of the incident. This war and conflict in Saudi Arabia is not a new issue, but has been ongoing for the past two years. Despite the high risk of war and attack, Nepalis are being forced to go abroad for employment without even caring for their lives due to poverty and severe economic constraints within the country. The future of millions of Nepalis traveling to Saudi Arabia will be determined by the strategy the government adopts in the coming days, keeping in mind the security situation, and how the international situation progresses.
